about.title: Laguna Niguel Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Orange County traffic records show Laguna Niguel saw 3 traffic deaths alongside 107 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, with reported crashes clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. along corridors like Crown Valley Parkway, Golden Lantern, Alicia Parkway, and Moulton Parkway. Behind every one of those numbers is a family trying to understand what comes next. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs sometimes eligible if none of those close relatives survive. These cases are separate from any criminal proceeding and follow their own civil timeline. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects grieving families in Laguna Niguel with an independent attorney who can explain your options, evaluate what happened, and walk beside you through a difficult process, all without any upfront cost to your family.

whyChoose.title: What Laguna Niguel Families Should Know

items.title: Standing Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California restricts who may file, generally prioritizing a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs and lost financial support, along with compensation for the loss of a loved one's companionship, guidance, and care, losses that are real even without a dollar receipt.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Laguna Niguel?
items.answer: Generally, California gives surviving family members two years from the date of death to file a civil wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as a public roadway agency, may be involved, that deadline can be much shorter and require an early formal claim. An attorney can review the specifics and confirm the timeline that applies to your case.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file this kind of claim?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a spouse, domestic partner, or children of the person who died. If none of those relatives exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing to bring the claim. Because these rules can be complex, it helps to have an attorney review your family's situation directly.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that may arise from the same collision. Given that Laguna Niguel sees crash activity along corridors like Crown Valley Parkway and Golden Lantern, especially on Friday afternoons, a civil claim can move forward independently of, and on a different timeline than, any police investigation or prosecution.

items.question: Is there any cost to speak with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out simply connects you with someone who can answer questions and explain your options.
